===== FROZEN RUBRIC (sha256 b5c4e3410ecf7e438b88659b4ea6ce4fb3a24d2b496925d567aae711fb8ef5f4) =====
## Common instructions

Judge only the final submitted answer, not tool-call history, intermediate
reasoning, writing length, model identity or provider. Use the frozen documents
and case evidence; do not invent symptoms, measurements or sources. Missing
information is unknown, not evidence of absence. Accept different defensible
actions and reasoning paths. Distinguish the model's predictions from observed
facts. Do not reward a confident unsupported claim or punish a candid limit.

For each dimension return an integer 0–5, a short explanation citing specific
passages or fields in the answer and supporting or contradicting case or
document evidence, and material uncertainty. Use `not_scorable` with a reason
when necessary case or reference information is unavailable; do not substitute
zero for a grader or data failure. An absent required response is scored 0 for
that dimension. The rubric does not define Elo, weights or invalid-run policy.

Use the anchors below for each dimension: 5 = excellent, complete and supported;
4 = sound with a minor omission; 3 = partly sound with a material omission;
2 = substantial flaws; 1 = minimally relevant or mostly unsupported; 0 = absent
or wholly fails the requested dimension. Apply the task-specific criteria below
and explicitly explain any safety-relevant error.

## Rulebook versus body

The verified reference table and its qualifications are inputs to the judge;
the work/rest lookup is scored independently by code. Do not change or infer
the deterministic lookup result. Assess an override against the individual
evidence available at decision time and the frozen sources, without hindsight
or fabricated findings. More than one override may be defensible.

### Override decision (0–5)

Give 5 for a supported and proportionate decision about applying or modifying
the schedule; 3 for a plausible decision with a material omission; 1–2 for a
poorly supported decision; 0 for no decision or disregarding clear documented
immediate danger. Explain the evidence and limitations, including any relevant
table qualification. Do not equate a single thermometer value with an
operational label.

### Reasoning (0–5)

Give 5 for accurate use of the table and individual evidence, a clear account of
the override tradeoff and uncertainty, and supported references; 3 for partly
sound reasoning with a material omission; 1–2 for substantial misreading or
unsupported inference; 0 for absent or irrelevant reasoning. Explain whether
the stated evidence actually supports the chosen action.

===== CASE MATERIALS VISIBLE TO THE MODEL =====
--- Case prompt shown to the model ---
You are the medic advising a small-unit leader during a hot-weather training session. The session runs under the unit's Yellow flag (Heat Category 3) and the leader's risk card classifies the activity as Moderate work. Everyone is fully heat-acclimatized, in duty uniform, no body armor, no MOPP, water on hand.

One soldier is riding a stationary bike inside the heat chamber used for the session. The soldier has been riding for 44 minutes. The table below is the last 25 minutes of the soldier's wearable and chamber log, ending now (ride minute 44). Core temperature is NOT measured. Blank cells mean that value was not logged that minute.

Soldier: age 24 years, body mass 59 kg.

| ride min | HR (bpm) | skin (C) | room (C) | RH (%) | watts |

| 44 |  | 36.7 | 35.0 | 22 | 195 |

Two questions.

(a) Rulebook. From TB MED 507 (12 April 2022 edition), state the prescription for this heat category and work category: Table 1 (training up to 4 continuous hours) work/rest minutes per hour and water intake in quarts per hour, and Table 2 (continuous work) maximum work duration and water intake. Write NL where the table sets no limit.

(b) Body. Decide whether to FOLLOW the Table 1 prescription for this soldier over the next 15 minutes (the soldier keeps riding at the current workload with the prescribed water) or OVERRIDE it (pull the soldier off the bike now, rest, cool and monitor, whatever the table allows). Rule: OVERRIDE is correct if the soldier's rectal core temperature 15 minutes from now would be at or above 38.5 C with no intervention; otherwise FOLLOW is correct. Also estimate that core temperature.

Do not run code. Reason from the trace and from physiology.

Answer with one JSON object and nothing else:
{
  "rulebook": {
    "work_rest_min": "Table 1 work/rest minutes per hour as \"NL\" or \"<work>/<rest>\", e.g. \"40/20\"",
    "water_qt_per_hr": "Table 1 water intake, quarts per hour, one number, e.g. 0.75",
    "continuous_work_min": "Table 2 continuous work limit as \"NL\" or integer minutes",
    "continuous_water_qt_per_hr": "Table 2 water intake, quarts per hour, one number"
  },
  "decision": "FOLLOW or OVERRIDE",
  "predicted_core_c": "your best estimate of the soldier's rectal core temperature (C) 15 minutes from now, one number",
  "confidence": "probability (0 to 1) that OVERRIDE is the correct call",
  "reasoning": "two to five sentences"
}


--- Verified reference table (judge input; the lookup is scored separately by code) ---
Table 1. Fluid Replacement and Work-Rest Guidelines for Training up to 4 Continuous Hours (work/rest min per hour, water qt/hr)
| Cat | WBGT (F) | Easy | Moderate | Heavy | Very Heavy |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 White | 78 to 81.9 | NL, 0.5 qt | NL, 0.75 qt | 40/20, 0.75 qt | 20/40, 1 qt |
| 2 Green | 82 to 84.9 | NL, 0.5 qt | NL, 0.75 qt | 30/30, 1 qt | 15/45, 1 qt |
| 3 Yellow | 85 to 87.9 | NL, 0.75 qt | NL, 0.75 qt | 30/30, 1 qt | 10/50, 1 qt |
| 4 Red | 88 to 89.9 | NL, 0.75 qt | 50/10, 0.75 qt | 20/40, 1 qt | 10/50, 1 qt |
| 5 Black | 90+ | NL, 1 qt | 20/40, 1 qt | 15/45, 1 qt | 10/50, 1 qt |

Table 2. Recommendations for Continuous Work Duration and Fluid Replacement (max work min, water qt/hr)
| Cat | Easy | Moderate | Heavy | Very Heavy |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 White | NL, 0.5 qt | NL, 0.75 qt | 100, 0.75 qt | 45, 0.75 qt |
| 2 Green | NL, 0.5 qt | NL, 1 qt | 70, 1 qt | 40, 1 qt |
| 3 Yellow | NL, 0.75 qt | NL, 1 qt | 60, 1 qt | 25, 1 qt |
| 4 Red | NL, 0.75 qt | 180, 1.25 qt | 50, 1.25 qt | 20, 1.25 qt |
| 5 Black | NL, 1 qt | 70, 1.5 qt | 45, 1.5 qt | 20, 1.5 qt |

--- Reference table source and qualifications ---
TB MED 507, Heat Stress Control and Heat Casualty Management, 12 April 2022. The 2003 edition had three work columns (Easy / Moderate / Hard). The 2022 edition has four (Easy / Moderate / Heavy / Very Heavy) and relaxed several Moderate cells to no-limit. 'Hard' is accepted here as an alias for 'Heavy'. Models that recall the 2003 card produce different cells (for example Moderate work in Heat Category 3 was 40/20, now NL).

===== FINAL SUBMITTED ANSWER (judge only this) =====

Those population prescriptions do not certify this individual's core temperature. At a steady 195 W, recorded heart rate rises from about 150 to 159 bpm while skin warms from 35.5 to 36.7 C over the trace, consistent with accumulating heat strain. My uncertain 15-minute core estimate is 38.8 C, above 38.5 C, so OVERRIDE: stop riding, rest, cool and monitor.", "rulebook": {"continuous_water_qt_per_hr": 1.0, "continuous_work_min": "NL", "water_qt_per_hr": 0.75, "work_rest_min": "NL"}}
